findings.claim: The round-2 repair booked its own corroboration one notch stronger than the page supports: paragraph 5 now asserts that Vestrigg agrees the forecast over-calls, but her only quoted words are direction-neutral about over- versus under-calling, and the agreement is reported rather than shown.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 5, inserted in round 2 and re-worded in 2b: “That the forecast asks for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings, and the forecast’s own author reads it the same way, but it is a reading of the empty frames and not a count taken from them.” Vestrigg’s only quotation, paragraph 3: “The layers are usually shallow enough that one step down is out of them,” “Which night, and which fifty miles of the route – that is what we get wrong.” Her only other reported position, paragraph 5: “Vestrigg wants humidity sensors flying on the airliners themselves, a hundred of them to begin with, and believes the rest would follow.” The repair_log (round 2, edit 1) states the intended chain explicitly: “corroborated from outside the imagery by the forecast’s own author, who says in paragraph 3 which night and which fifty miles is what they get wrong”.
findings.why: Getting “which night, and which fifty miles” wrong is a placement error, and placement errors produce false alarms and misses in equal measure; wanting better humidity sensors likewise says the input is thin, not that the output is biased in one direction. Neither quoted position asserts the asymmetry (asks-for-more-than-the-sky-supplies) that the sentence says she shares. The repair's other corroboration is sound and stands: the 141 control flights establish an 80-empty-frame base rate under NO intervention, which is why success cannot explain the empties and the forecast can. The Vestrigg clause is therefore a redundant reinforcement that outruns its own quotations rather than a load-bearing error.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. No key depends on it. Q5/A turns on the writer’s ranking of imagery against center records, Q5/B on Vestrigg’s sensor wish being hers and not his, and Q4/C on paragraph 4’s flat writer’s-voice sentence “The forecast was calling for wet air a good deal more often than the sky supplied it” – all three are untouched by this clause. Authorial report of a source’s position is normal in the genre, and no question asks the student to derive her agreement from her quotation. If any editorial pass is spent on this unit, the minimal fix is to soften to “and the forecast’s own author does not dispute it” or to drop the clause; both are within the 15-word band headroom (see VF2-10).

findings.claim: The 2b re-wording of G-ENG’s “points the same way” finding introduced a pronoun that carries two different referents inside one sentence.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 5: “That the forecast asks for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings, and the forecast’s own author reads it the same way, but it is a reading of the empty frames and not a count taken from them.” First “it” = the evidence being read (the empty pictures; the nearest plural noun, “the empty frames”, cannot antecede a singular). Second “it” = the fronted that-clause, i.e. the reading itself. G-ENG run 1 had proposed “and the forecast’s own author says as much”, which has no pronoun.
findings.why: G-ENG’s finding was the personal-collocation slip (a person cannot “point the same way”); the 2b substitution cures that but pays for it with an antecedent wobble the original did not have. “Read it the same way” is idiomatic with a vague situational “it”, so the sentence is recoverable on a first pass, but the same sentence then re-uses “it” for a different thing eleven words later.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Cosmetic, recoverable, passage-layer only, no key impact – both blind G-KEY legs and this audit’s cold solve read paragraph 5 correctly with the sentence in place. Note for the record that this is a 2b-introduced wrinkle, not a pre-existing one, and that G-ENG’s own suggested wording would have avoided it; the orchestrator’s ticket describes the 2b edits as applied “verbatim”, which is accurate for edits 1 and 3 but not for this one.

findings.claim: RECONCILED, NOT CONVICTED – the paragraph-4 population tension escalated by G-DISTRACTOR. 406 step-down plans minus 96 flown leaves 310 traded away, and a traded-away step-down leaves an airplane where it would have been anyway; yet the audit sentence counts only 141 flights that “were left alone and flew straight through a forecast layer”. The two populations are consistent because the passage never claims the 141 exhausts the unmoved crossings.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 4, first number: “Of 141 flights that were left alone and flew straight through a forecast layer, 61 left a mark anybody could find afterward.” Paragraph 4, second number: “Of 406 plans written with the step-down in them, 96 were flown that way; the rest were traded away for traffic, for weather, for a crew that wanted the fuel.” Paragraph 3, the treatment rule: “On nights when the forecast laid one of these layers across a route, the flight was planned two thousand feet beneath it”. generator_meta.self_blind_solve (round-2 addendum) computes the residual independently: “nothing about the 310 plans that were traded away”.
findings.why: Two readings of the page both close the arithmetic, and the passage licenses either. (i) DISJOINT ARMS. “Left alone” is a deliberate designation – flights the center chose not to plan a step-down for – and the 406 are the treatment arm. On this reading the sector handled at least 547 forecast-layer crossings: 141 designated controls, 406 planned, 96 flown as planned, 310 planned-then-traded. The 310 are a third, contaminated population (traded “for weather” can mean a reroute, “for traffic” a different assigned level, so many of them did not fly straight through the layer at all) whose detection outcomes the passage simply does not report – and which no clean audit would pool with a control arm. (ii) NESTED. The 141 are those of the 310 that demonstrably ended up flying straight through the forecast layer, the remainder having been rerouted or re-levelled. Under both readings every number on the page is true and no sentence is contradicted. What the passage does NOT say – and what would be needed to convict – is that 141 is the complete count of unmoved crossings. It states a population, as operational audits routinely do; it does not state a partition.
findings.disposition: NO DEFECT. Ruled reconcilable, not a defect, and no key is exposed to the ambiguity. Tested directly against Q4, the only item that reads this paragraph: A (“Fewer than half of them were flying where the forecast had put a layer”) is false under every reading, because ALL 141 are stated in the same sentence to have flown through a forecast layer and it is the marks, not the flights, that are fewer than half; B reverses a documented false positive into a false negative under every reading; D is settled by the 61 marks under every reading; C (the key) follows from the 61-of-141 hit rate plus the fact that the flown descents were planned on the same forecast, and holds identically whether the 310 are a third arm or the 141’s parent set. Both fresh blind G-KEY legs returned C with the same chain and neither reported the tension as a solving obstacle. Recorded here so the escalation is answered on the record rather than left standing.

findings.claim: Twelve of G-ENG’s fifteen round-2 findings were not applied in 2b and are still present verbatim in the shipping bytes. All twelve are single-run (1 of 3) minors in the rationale layer; the one finding that reached 3-of-3 consensus was the only major and it was fixed.
findings.evidence: Verified present in candidates-final bytes: (1) “so a large share of them were made into air that would have produced nothing anyway” [Q4, garden path]; (2) “The reader supplies the join” [Q3, BrE noun in an AmE-declared unit]; (3) “says that the two oppose, not which of them wins” [Q3, bare intransitive]; (4) “cannot be answered with a thing the text conspicuously leaves open” [Q3, register]; (5) “and it is not time-of-day dependent” [Q3, unhyphenated compound modifier]; (6) “WHY-KEY (C): 141 airplanes were sent” [Q4, numeral-initial sentence]; (7) “and the word cool is never used of a contrail” and “Worthless is a word for evidence that says nothing either way” [Q3/Q5, unmarked use-mention]; (8) “many of the descents rather than all of them, and will have bought nothing rather than bought nothing” [Q4, four unmarked mentions in one clause]; (9) “where he names among the findings that will outlast the trial” [Q4, name + bare that-clause]; (10) “a forecast asking for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings” [Q4, category slip: the passage fronts a that-clause, the paraphrase predicates “reading” of the forecast]; (11) “Perhaps it would.” [passage, pronoun number after “the rest”]; (12) “the trial, the audit and the counting” against “cannot see a young contrail, cannot see its height, and cannot tell four or five tracks apart” [Q1, serial-comma inconsistency inside one rationale]. Applied and verified landed in 2b: “spend room on” -> “give room to” (3/3 major), the fault-partition clause, and “points the same way” -> “reads it the same way”.
findings.why: Frequency is the discriminator. G-ENG ran three independent legs; exactly one finding recurred in all three, and it was a genuine non-collocation in newly written text. Every other finding appears once, and several are contested by the record itself: item (11) is conceded defensible by the flagging run (“the rest” as a singular remainder is standard, and the echo “Perhaps it would” tracks that construal), and items (7), (8) and (12) are house-style preferences with no single correct answer. None of the twelve touches a stem, an option, a key or a factual claim about the passage; eleven of the twelve are in the rationale layer, and the twelfth is defensible as written.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS, carried as a known-residual list. Ship-readiness does not turn on single-run stylistic preferences in the teaching payload, and the marginal risk of another rationale rewrite is higher than the marginal gain: two repair rounds have already churned this text, and the audit that follows a third would have to re-run the full quote-fidelity sweep to certify no new orphan was created. Recommended, if a batch-level copy pass is ever run: (10) and (6), which are the only two with any substantive content – (10) because it mis-predicates a category the unit elsewhere polices, (6) because numeral-initial sentences are a house rule the rest of the corpus keeps.

findings.claim: PARTIAL REFUTATION of G-ENG’s quotation-punctuation finding. G-ENG recorded the rationale layer as internally split – “10 of 11 rationale instances go BrE, 1 goes AmE”. Measured on the final bytes, the rationale layer is 100 percent internally consistent; the single instance G-ENG counted as AmE is a complete-sentence quotation, where AmE and BrE agree. The real residual is a passage-versus-rationale layer split, not an inconsistency inside either layer.
findings.evidence: Passage: 4 of 4 terminal marks inside the closing quote (AmE typesetting), 0 outside. Rationale layer: 10 partial-phrase quotations, all 10 with the mark outside the closing quote (BrE logical style), e.g. Q2 “...leaves crossing it”. and Q5 “...those two winters produced”,. The eleventh instance, Q3, is “it also turns some sunlight back toward space, so the two effects pull against one another, while after dark there is nothing pulling the other way.” – a complete quoted sentence carrying its own terminal period inside the quotes, which is correct in both varieties and therefore not an AmE outlier. generator_meta.spelling_variety is AmE; a scan of passage plus all five rationales, prompts and twenty options finds AmE spelling throughout (center 6, airplane 15, toward 3, among 1; zero BrE spellings, zero -ise forms outside “premise” / “otherwise” / “cruising”).
findings.why: The substantive risk that AmE quotation typesetting carries is that it puts inside the quotation marks a mark the source did not write. That risk is taken only by the passage, which is fiction and its own source, and never by the rationale layer, which quotes the passage and keeps every mark outside – so no quotation in the teaching payload is misrepresented by its punctuation. The residual is a house-style seam between two layers, visible only to a copy editor.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. Cosmetic, does not corrupt a single quotation, and does not touch spelling variety, which is cleanly AmE. Checked across the batch for pattern: no other unit in batch17 has more than two quoted terminal marks in its rationale layer, so this is a consequence of this unit quoting unusually heavily rather than a batch-wide drift needing a policy edit. If a house rule is ever set, set it batch-wide and regenerate; do not one-off patch this unit.

findings.claim: The 2b fault-partition clause is arithmetically correct but mixes three constructions and indexes “the fourth” against the partition it is building rather than against the order in which the passage listed the four causes.
findings.evidence: The list, paragraph 5: “And a success looks like an empty picture. So does a forecast that was wrong, and a contrail too thin to register, and a sheet of cloud sitting over the top of one.” The 2b partition, two sentences later: “An empty one settles nothing, and only one of the readings it allows blames the forecast; two are the camera’s, and the fourth is the success the flight was after.” Arithmetic verified against the list: forecast-was-wrong = 1; too-thin-to-register plus overlying-cloud-sheet = 2 (both instrument limits); success = 1; total 4, matching the four causes exactly, with no cause double-counted and none left over.
findings.why: Two small seams. (a) The three clauses take three shapes – a finite verb (“blames the forecast”), an elliptical possessive (“are the camera’s”), and an identity (“is the success”) – so the parallelism the sentence is doing arithmetic with is not carried by its syntax. (b) Success is item one in the passage’s own list and is called “the fourth” here; the ordinal indexes the running total inside this sentence (1 + 2 = 3, so the remaining one is the fourth), not the list order, and a reader tracking the earlier list meets a momentary mismatch.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS, and record that the 2b edit is a net improvement on what G-ENG flagged. G-ENG’s own proposed wording (“the rest blame the camera”) would have preserved the mis-count the orchestrator was fixing – it assigns success to the camera – so the deviation from “verbatim” here was correct and the honest count is the right call. The residual is a reading speed-bump, not an error, and the arithmetic it carries is the load-bearing part and is right.

findings.claim: Q2’s WHY-KEY opens on a count the paragraph does not quite support: “paragraph 2 gives exactly two properties”.
findings.evidence: Q2 rationale: “WHY-KEY (A): paragraph 2 gives exactly two properties.” Paragraph 2 in fact states supersaturation (“Air can sit well past ice saturation”), absence of cloud (“make no cloud of its own”, “nothing in it to look at”), horizontal extent (“runs a couple of hundred miles”) and depth (“a depth that would fit inside a small hill”).
findings.why: Defensible as a grouping – invisibility as one property and geometry as another, with supersaturation arguably the layer’s definition rather than a further property, and introduced in paragraph 1 – but “exactly” is a strong word for a count a student can contest in five seconds, and rationale claims that are checkable-and-wrong are precisely what round 1 convicted on Q1/C. This one is checkable-and-arguable, which is a much weaker charge: the two properties the rationale then names are both quoted verbatim from the paragraph and both are in key A.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. No student harm – A’s two claims (shallow, no cloud) are each supported by a verbatim quotation in the same rationale, and the count is a framing sentence rather than a load-bearing one. Softening “exactly two properties” to “two properties” would close it at zero risk if an editorial pass is spent.

findings.claim: Q3’s refutation of distractor A claims exclusivity it does not have, and in doing so passes over the passage’s stronger refutation of the same option.
findings.evidence: Q3 rationale: “the text’s only remark about how busy the sky is comes later and cuts the other way, since on a busy evening four or five tracks cross the same square.” Paragraph 4 also remarks on traffic, and does so decisively against option A (“Traffic after dark was light enough for the center to move the airplanes freely”): “the rest were traded away for traffic, for weather, for a crew that wanted the fuel.” Both fresh blind G-KEY legs used the paragraph-4 sentence when putting A down; leg 2 cites it explicitly.
findings.why: Paragraph 4 shows traffic actively taking descents away from the center, which contradicts “freely” outright, where paragraph 5’s busy evening only points the other way by implication. So the rationale (a) makes an “only” claim that is inaccurate and (b) teaches the weaker of the two available refutations. The trap label and the key are unaffected: A is wrong on both sentences, not merely unsupported.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. The item is if anything safer than its rationale claims – a distractor contradicted twice is not a distractor at risk. Recommended one-clause improvement if an editorial pass is spent: cite “traded away for traffic” first and the busy evening second, and drop “only”.

findings.claim: Q4’s refutation of distractor B rests on a study-design statement the passage does not make.
findings.evidence: Q4 rationale: “B = the reversal, and the sharpest distractor here: a false negative offered where the passage documents a false positive. Nothing in the trial could have found a layer the forecast failed to call, because only called layers were flown through on purpose.” The passage never says any flight was routed through a layer on purpose; it says flights were “left alone” and “flew straight through a forecast layer”.
findings.why: The operative logic is sound and does not need the extra claim: the audited population is defined by having flown through a FORECAST layer, so an uncalled layer is outside the measured set by construction, and the passage documents over-calling (“The forecast was calling for wet air a good deal more often than the sky supplied it”) and never a miss. “On purpose” is a mild over-specification of the design – though “left alone” does connote a deliberate control arm, which is why this reads as imprecision rather than invention.
findings.disposition: SHIP AS IS. B is indefensible on the page regardless, and both blind G-KEY legs put it down by direction-of-error alone without needing any design claim. Minimal fix if an editorial pass is spent: “because only layers the forecast had already called were ever audited”.

findings.claim: The unit ships at two band ceilings. Any third repair that inserts prose into the passage risks an M-BANDS kill rather than a note.
findings.evidence: Mechanical gates re-run by this audit on the FINAL post-2b bytes (run_mech.py, --parsed-dir data/parsed): M-SCHEMA pass, M-BANDS pass, M-TELL pass, M-FORM pass, M-PLAGIARISM pass. Measured: 858 tokens against the ELF long_passage band [332, 873] – 15 tokens of headroom; 5 paragraphs against a maximum of 5 – zero headroom; 38 sentences, mean 22.58 words, band [14.9, 35.4]. Round 2 added +92 tokens and 2b a further +8.
findings.why: The round-2 repair already had to place its new material inside existing paragraphs rather than add a sixth, because the paragraph ceiling was reached. A further insertion of the size of round 2’s (+76 tokens for the epistemics block alone) would exceed the word ceiling outright.
findings.disposition: INFORMATIONAL, no action. Recorded as a constraint on any future repair of this unit: word-count-neutral or word-count-negative edits only, and no new paragraph. Every fix recommended elsewhere in this audit is inside the 15-token headroom or reduces length.

findings.claim: ARTIFACT SHAPE, NOT UNIT DEFECT. The round-2 blind G-KEY legs omit the “vote” field that the round-1 legs carried. vfinal_fold.py de-duplicates on (gate, target, vote), so with vote absent the two independent legs collapse to one record per question and the derived record will report gkey_records=5 where the evidence on disk is 10.
findings.evidence: verdicts-r2/verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl and -2.jsonl (5 lines each) and verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl (10 lines) carry keys [candidate_id, date, executed_by, findings, gate, justification, solver_answer, target, verdict] – no “vote”. The round-1 legs in verdicts-vfinal/ do carry “vote”: 1 and “vote”: 2. vfinal_fold.py._last_wins keys on (v.get(“gate”), v.get(“target”), v.get(“vote”)). Simulated fold on the r2 directory: gkey_records=5, kills=0, flags=0.
findings.why: For THIS unit nothing is lost in substance: this audit read all ten raw records by hand and both legs are complete and identical – q1 B, q2 A, q3 D, q4 C, q5 A, twice, every line “pass”, zero findings – so whichever record survives the collapse is a pass and the fold verdict is unaffected. gkey_resolve.py is also unaffected, because it indexes siblings on (candidate_id, target) rather than on vote, so the split-vote rule saw both legs and resolved them with full cross-vote context. The reason to record it is the latent direction of the failure: had the two legs disagreed, gkey_resolve would have marked the dissenting line “flag” and its sibling “pass”, and the vote-blind collapse would keep only the later of the two – so a dissent recorded earlier in the file would vanish from the fold entirely, taking gkey_flags to 0 and deriving VERIFIED where VERIFIED_NOTES is owed. That is a fail-open in a chain whose stated design principle is fail-closed.
findings.disposition: NO IMPACT ON THIS UNIT’S SHIP-READINESS; orchestration item, outside this audit’s write boundary (this audit writes only audits/elf-b17-001.json). Recommended before the fold is regenerated: stamp “vote”: 1 / “vote”: 2 on verdicts-r2/verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl and -2.jsonl, re-run gkey_resolve.py over them, and point vfinal_fold.py at --verdicts-dir verdicts-r2 rather than verdicts-vfinal – the runbook’s example command names verdicts-vfinal, which for this batch now holds the STALE round-1 legs read against pre-repair bytes. Those stale legs are also all-pass, so the verdict does not change either way, but the fold should certify the fresh legs, not the superseded ones.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Paragraph 5 named four distinct causes of an empty picture, one of which is the forecast being wrong, then treated the control flights’ no-detection results as if they had established that the forecast was wrong, and called that finding a product of paperwork – “Both of those come off records the center already keeps” – when only the 96-of-406 take rate comes off center paperwork.
resolved_findings.repair: Round 2, two edits. (1) Three sentences inserted immediately after the four-causes list: “A picture that shows a contrail settles that one flight. An empty one settles nothing, and only one of the readings it allows blames the forecast; two are the camera’s, and the fourth is the success the flight was after. That the forecast asks for more than the sky supplies is the best of those readings, and the forecast’s own author reads it the same way, but it is a reading of the empty frames and not a count taken from them.” (2) “Both of those come off records the center already keeps.” -> “The second of those comes off records the center already keeps and needed no picture at all.” (Clause wording in (1) as finalised by 2b.)
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED. Verified on the final bytes by this audit. (a) The false sentence is gone: “Both of those come off” is absent, “The second of those comes off” is present. (b) The referent is right: “those” points at the two findings named in the previous sentence, and the second of them (“most of the descents it asks for are never flown”) is exactly the 96-of-406 take rate, which is pure center paperwork – plans written against plans flown, no imagery involved. (c) The first finding is no longer smuggled into the paperwork claim; it is explicitly booked as “a reading of the empty frames and not a count taken from them”, which is the strongest thing the evidence licenses. (d) The four-cause partition now closes: 1 forecast + 2 camera + 1 success = the four causes listed, verified item by item (see VF2-06). (e) The epistemic asymmetry the block asserts is sound and is the reason the ranking survives: every limitation named in paragraph 5 can hide a contrail and none can manufacture one, so a positive frame is informative about that flight and an empty frame is not – which is precisely what “A picture that shows a contrail settles that one flight. An empty one settles nothing” says. (f) Independent corroboration from paragraph 4 that the repair does not itself claim: the 141 controls were NOT manoeuvred, so their 80 empty frames cannot be successes, which is why the forecast-over-calls reading is the best of the four. The residual on the Vestrigg corroboration clause is carried forward as VF2-01 at minor.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Q1’s WHY-DISTRACTORS made two false statements about the passage to dismiss option C: that crystal growth is “disposed of in a single clause of paragraph 1”, and that it “matters here only because it explains why the layer is invisible”.
resolved_findings.repair: Round 2 rewrote Q1/C’s entry onto the real defect (a premise promoted to subject) and widened the trap label to “surface_word_match over a part-for-whole scope error”; 2b replaced the collocation “spend room on” with “give room to”. The false “single clause” characterisation was also retracted by name in generator_meta.self_blind_solve.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED. Both false statements are absent from the final bytes. The replacements are checkable and check out: crystal growth is the back half of paragraph 1, running from “Usually that air is dry with respect to ice” to “It came out of the air the airplane was passing through” (4 of the paragraph’s 7 sentences); paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 do not touch crystal growth; paragraph 2 returns to crystals only for the nucleation gap (“starting a crystal from nothing needs roughly half again as much vapor as keeping an existing one alive”), which is a different mechanism doing a different job, exactly as the rewritten rationale now says. generator_meta.question_families, question_geometry and engineered_traps all carry the widened label, so no refiling survives in one place only. The retraction in self_blind_solve is present and names the round-1 line it retracts.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Q3’s WHY-DISTRACTORS defeated option C with outside knowledge, asserting that the passage states a partial cancellation and therefore a net sign, which the passage never does.
resolved_findings.repair: Round 2 replaced the refutation with a wholly within-passage one turning on two words the reader can see (“also” and “pull against”) plus the stem’s own “told”.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED. The replacement asserts no sign: “no sentence anywhere in the text delivers a net verdict for daylight, and the word cool is never used of a contrail” – both verified, warm/warming, cool/cooling and climate each occur 0 times in the final passage. It closes on the correct line, which is entailment: “a stem asking what we are told cannot be answered with a thing the text conspicuously leaves open”. Checked for the same error surviving elsewhere in the unit: the round-1 self_blind_solve line on Q3/C reads “partial cancellation and says nothing about which side wins”, which already disclaims the sign and is therefore not the convicted move; the round-2 addendum re-argues C without the phrase (“the repaired paragraph 3 still declines to give one”). No unretracted instance of the convicted claim survives anywhere in the file.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Q3’s key D leaned on “the warming”, whose first member the passage never introduced (“the two effects” had an antecedent for its second member only); the rationale claimed D “adds nothing”; and the item was filed as ELF-TYPE-001 direct detail retrieval while requiring a joining step.
resolved_findings.repair: Round 2 named the first effect in the passage’s own register without using the word warming (“Nights only: a spreading contrail holds in heat that would otherwise leave, and in daylight it also turns some sunlight back toward space, so the two effects pull against one another, while after dark there is nothing pulling the other way.”), rewrote WHY-KEY to state what the reader must supply, and refiled the item to ELF-TYPE-002 in the rationale, in question_families and in question_geometry.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED, and Q3’s key licensing independently re-derived by this audit from the amended paragraph 3. D reads “After dark nothing works against the warming, since no sunlight is turned away.” Each part is now on the page: “the warming” <- “holds in heat that would otherwise leave” (one re-description, no imported term); “nothing works against” <- “there is nothing pulling the other way”; “since no sunlight is turned away” <- “in daylight it also turns some sunlight back toward space” plus the night-versus-daylight contrast the sentence is built on. “Also” now has something to add to, and “the two effects” now has an antecedent for both members – the defect is closed at its root. The ELF-TYPE-002 refiling is correct and consistent in all three places: D is one join plus one re-description, which is the family’s one-logical-inch shape, and the two inference items in the unit sit in different paragraphs and perform different operations (a join in 3, a consequence in 4). “Adds nothing” is gone. Both fresh blind G-KEY legs returned D on the repaired sentence, and this audit’s cold solve returned D independently. One observation carried, not a finding: the stem’s “told” does double duty, licensing an entailment for D while excluding a non-entailed verdict for C. The line between them is entailment, the rationale draws it (“conspicuously leaves open”), and the item is sound.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Q1/C rationale, newly written in round 2: “it names something the text really does spend room on” – a non-collocation, “have room for” crossed with “spend time/space on”. Flagged by all three G-ENG legs, the only finding to reach consensus.
resolved_findings.repair: 2b: -> “it names something the text really does give room to”.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED, landed correctly, no new defect. “spend room on” is absent from the final bytes; “give room to” is present and is idiomatic in exactly this sense (a text gives room to a topic). The surrounding sentence is unchanged and still says what the repair intended: the trap is proportion, not accuracy.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Paragraph 5, newly written in round 2: “only one of the readings it allows is the forecast’s fault; the rest are the camera’s” – a reading cannot be a fault, and the sentence silently swaps interpretation for cause.
resolved_findings.repair: 2b: -> “only one of the readings it allows blames the forecast; two are the camera’s, and the fourth is the success the flight was after”. This DEPARTS from G-ENG’s proposed wording (“the rest blame the camera”), which the orchestrator disclosed as a mis-count fix.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED, and the departure was correct. G-ENG’s own rewrite would have re-introduced a substantive error – it assigns all three non-forecast readings to the camera, but one of the four is the success the flight was after, which is neither the forecast’s doing nor the camera’s. The applied wording counts honestly (1 forecast + 2 camera + 1 success) and this audit verified the partition item by item against the four causes as listed; no cause is double-counted and none is left over. The idiom complaint is also cured: a reading that blames something is idiomatic. Residual construction seams carried forward as VF2-06 at note.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Paragraph 5, newly written in round 2: “the forecast’s own author points the same way” – “point the same way” collocates with evidence or findings, not with a person.
resolved_findings.repair: 2b: -> “the forecast’s own author reads it the same way”. G-ENG had proposed “says as much”.

cleared.item: COLD SOLVE, all five, keys covered
cleared.result: 5 of 5 matching. Q1=B, Q2=A, Q3=D, Q4=C, Q5=A, against the shipped key string B A D C A. Solved from the final passage before reading any rationale, arguing each non-keyed option for before putting it down. Q1: B names both halves the piece is built from – a cheap manoeuvre (two thousand feet, ~2 percent per flight, a fraction of a percent per sector) and an evidence problem that fills the last paragraph; A and C are strands, D is a comparison never made. Q2: A’s two claims are both stated; B is the paragraph’s reversal, C is refuted by “the first anyone knows of it is the mark an airplane leaves crossing it”, D moves the contrail’s verb onto the layer. Q3: D joins the two named effects, A is contradicted by paragraph 4’s traffic trade-aways, B invents a depth comparison, C supplies a net sign the text withholds. Q4: C follows from 61 of 141 plus the descents being planned on the same forecast; A misreads the denominator, B reverses the error direction, D dies on the 61 marks. Q5: A is the writer’s explicit ranking; B is Vestrigg’s wish, C is refuted by the ranking, D overshoots past the granted positive frame. No question yielded a second defensible option.

cleared.item: QUOTE FIDELITY across two rounds of passage churn
cleared.result: ZERO ORPHANS. 19 quoted spans across the five rationales, extracted mechanically and matched against the final passage: 18 resolve to the passage, 1 (“fewer than half”, Q4) is a quotation of the unit’s own distractor A and is correctly used as a mention. Two spans differ from the passage in initial capitalisation only, and both are standard editorial practice rather than misquotation: Q3’s sentence-initial mention of the word “Also” (passage: lower-case “also”), and Q5’s sentence-medial “a picture that shows a contrail settles that one flight” (passage: sentence-initial “A picture”). No quoted span survives from text the repairs deleted; specifically, the two spans that round 1 convicted as quoting a now-deleted sentence (Q5’s “Both of those come off records” and Q3’s pre-repair cut of the night-only sentence) are both gone and both replacements match the repaired passage word for word. Unquoted paraphrases were checked separately against the passage; the only loose one is G-ENG’s category slip in Q4, carried as VF2-04 item (10).

CONSISTENT. The four causes of an empty picture as listed (success / forecast wrong / too thin to register / overlying cloud sheet) map one-to-one onto the partition sentence (1 blames the forecast, 2 are the camera’s, the fourth is the success), with no cause double-counted or dropped. “The second of those” points unambiguously at the take-rate finding, which is genuinely paperwork-only. The first finding is explicitly NOT claimed as paperwork and is explicitly booked as a reading of the empty frames. The separate triple in Q1’s rationale (“cannot see a young contrail, cannot see its height, and cannot tell four or five tracks apart”) enumerates the satellite’s blindnesses, a different set from the four readings, and the two enumerations do not collide. The asymmetry the block rests on – every named limitation can hide a contrail, none can manufacture one – is sound, and paragraph 4 independently supplies the reason the forecast-over-calls reading beats the success reading: the 141 controls were never manoeuvred, so their 80 empty frames cannot be successes.

CLEAR. Proper nouns extracted mechanically from the passage: Sunniva Vestrigg, Anselm Colverdine, Lorcan Trawsfield – three personal names and nothing else. No place, country, airspace, airline, institution, satellite, aircraft type or publication is named anywhere in the passage, confirming generator_meta.fictional_entities. Web-verified: no real-world bearer for “Sunniva Vestrigg”, “Colverdine” (nearest attested surnames Colver, Colville, Coverdale, Cloverdine) or “Trawsfield” (nearest are Welsh place names Trawsfynydd, Trawsgoed, Trawsnant – different words, different referent class, no person or organisation). None of the three collides with a real bearer in this or any domain, so the aggravating class the law-16 report identifies (invented words attributed to a real person in the same field) is not engaged.

cleared.item: SCIENCE, spot-checked against the mechanism note’s own claims
cleared.result: No claim in the repaired text overreaches. Nucleation threshold (“roughly half again as much vapor”) matches homogeneous freezing at roughly 150 percent RHi against saturation for existing crystals; layer geometry (hundreds of miles across, depth “that would fit inside a small hill”) matches ice-supersaturated regions; the temperature-well-humidity-badly asymmetry, the two-thousand-foot step, the ~2 percent per-flight and fraction-of-a-percent fleet fuel penalty, the 5-minute-to-1-hour detection lag, the flat view carrying no altitude, and misattribution in dense traffic are all inside the verified set. Critically, the repaired paragraph 3 still refuses a net daylight sign, so the external morning-cooling result the unit’s own note concedes is left outside the passage rather than contradicted by it – which is what the round-1 MINOR-2 conviction required.
